# Fees and Payments Rules

Brindlecombe Community Boat Club is a fictional organisation.

## 1. Fees from 1 January 2026

### 1.1 Joining fee
A new member must pay a one-time joining fee of £15.

### 1.2 Annual individual fee
The annual fee for an individual membership is £55.

### 1.3 Annual household fee
The annual fee for a household membership is £85.

### 1.4 Annual junior fee
The annual fee for a junior membership is £25.

## 2. Renewal

### 2.1 Due date
Annual fees are due on 1 April each year.

### 2.2 Reminder
The Treasurer will send a reminder by 1 March where an email address is held.

### 2.3 Late payment
A membership becomes inactive on 15 April if the annual fee has not cleared.

## 3. Boat-use charges

### 3.1 Standard session
A booked rowing boat or kayak session costs £4 per boat.

### 3.2 Junior session
A session booked solely for junior members costs £2 per boat when an approved adult supervisor is present.

### 3.3 Payment timing
Boat-use charges must be paid before launch unless the Treasurer has agreed otherwise in writing.

## 4. Refunds

### 4.1 Club cancellation
The club will refund a boat-use charge in full if it cancels a confirmed booking.

### 4.2 Member cancellation
A member may receive a boat-use refund when cancelling at least 24 hours before the session start time.

### 4.3 No-show
No refund is due for a missed booking or a cancellation made less than 24 hours before its start time.

## 5. Other matters

### 5.1 Not covered
This document does not set insurance arrangements, donation policy, or prices for club social events.

# Boat Booking Rules

Brindlecombe Community Boat Club is a fictional organisation.

## 1. Who may book

### 1.1 Active members
Only an active member under boat-membership.md may make a booking.

### 1.2 Junior bookings
A junior member may book only where an approved adult member is named in the booking.

### 1.3 Guests
Guests cannot make bookings and must be included under the responsible member’s booking.

## 2. Booking window

### 2.1 Opening time
Bookings open at 8:00 am, 14 days before the session date.

### 2.2 Closing time
Bookings close two hours before the session start time.

### 2.3 Session length
A standard session lasts two hours, including launch and return time.

## 3. Limits

### 3.1 Weekly limit
A member may hold no more than three future bookings in any rolling seven-day period.

### 3.2 Boat limit
A member may book up to two boats in one session.

### 3.3 Priority
Committee-led training may reserve boats up to 21 days in advance.

## 4. Arrival and return

### 4.1 Arrival
The booking holder must arrive at least 10 minutes before launch.

### 4.2 Unclaimed boats
A boat may be released to another member 15 minutes after the booking start time.

### 4.3 Return
All boats must be returned, cleaned and secured before the session end time.

## 5. Cancellations

### 5.1 Member cancellation
Members must cancel promptly through the booking system or by contacting a committee member.

### 5.2 Fee refunds
Refund entitlement is determined by section 4 of boat-fees.md.

### 5.3 Unsafe conditions
A booking may be cancelled under section 4 of boat-safety.md.

# Water Safety Rules

Brindlecombe Community Boat Club is a fictional organisation.

## 1. Before launch

### 1.1 Buoyancy aids
Every person in a club boat must wear a properly fitted club-approved buoyancy aid.

### 1.2 Equipment check
The booking holder must check the boat, paddle or oars, and buoyancy aids before launch.

### 1.3 Defects
A boat with a suspected defect must not be launched and must be marked unavailable.

## 2. Young people

### 2.1 Under-12s
A child under 12 must share a boat with an adult member aged 18 or over.

### 2.2 Ages 12 to 17
A junior member aged 12 to 17 may use a boat only while an approved adult member remains on site.

### 2.3 Guest children
Guest children count toward the limits in section 4 of boat-membership.md.

## 3. Lake limits

### 3.1 Operating area
Club boats must remain within the marked boating area.

### 3.2 Distance
Boats must remain at least 10 metres from the reed beds and nesting platforms.

### 3.3 Night use
No club boat may be used from 30 minutes before sunset until sunrise.

## 4. Conditions

### 4.1 Closure authority
An on-duty committee member may close the lake to club boating because of wind, lightning, poor visibility, ice, water quality concerns or rescue activity.

### 4.2 Member decision
Members must not launch if they reasonably believe conditions are unsafe, even if the lake is open.

### 4.3 Cancellation
A closure cancels affected bookings for the purpose of section 4.1 of boat-fees.md.

## 5. Incidents

### 5.1 Immediate action
In an emergency, call the emergency services first where needed.

### 5.2 Reporting
All incidents, near misses and equipment failures must be reported to the Safety Officer within 24 hours.
